context.body: The most famous royal splendor becomes the lesser side of a comparison.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Jesus points to lilies clothed by God and says Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of them.
observations.label: Jesus compares lilies with Solomon’s glory: action

observations.body: Anxious hearers are directed from royal splendor to ordinary creation and divine care.
observations.label: Jesus compares lilies with Solomon’s glory: response

observations.body: lilies · Solomon in all his glory · God clothes
observations.label: Words in Matthew 6:28–30

payload.posture: Read Matthew 6:28–30 as later memory and aftermath evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The saying questions anxiety and status without claiming that beauty or royal work has no value.
payload.title: Jesus compares lilies with Solomon’s glory
